package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"path"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf16"

	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/ast"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/bundled"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/compiler"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/contentmapper"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/core"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/diagnostics"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/locale"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/parser"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/scanner"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/sourcemap"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/spanmap"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/tsoptions"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/tspath"
	"github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/tsc/internal/vfs/vfstest"
)

var compilerRevision = "unbound"
var compilerPatchSeries = "unbound"
var bridgeAPIVersion = "unbound"

// requestedComptimeTarget is the value `comptime.target` reports. The bridge
// serves exactly one request per process, so a request option is the whole
// lifetime of this value; it is never read from the environment, because an
// ambient value would make comptime evaluation observe host state.
var requestedComptimeTarget = defaultComptimeTarget

type loweredSource struct {
	Text      string `json:"text"`
	SourceMap string `json:"sourceMap"`
}

type sourceFile struct {
	Path    string         `json:"path"`
	Kind    string         `json:"kind"`
	Text    string         `json:"text"`
	Lowered *loweredSource `json:"lowered"`
}

type request struct {
	RootNames []string       `json:"rootNames"`
	Files     []sourceFile   `json:"files"`
	Options   map[string]any `json:"options"`
	Lowering  string         `json:"lowering"`
	// ConfigFile is the project's `tsconfig.json`, by name and text, when the
	// caller has one. It travels as TEXT rather than as a parsed options bag
	// because compatibility.mdx §Forbidden requires the offending option to be
	// REJECTED, and a rejection has to point at what the author wrote — a
	// normalized bag has no positions. Absent, the options map is still gated
	// by compilerOptions below; only the span is lost.
	ConfigFile *configFile `json:"configFile,omitempty"`
}

type configFile struct {
	Path string `json:"path"`
	Text string `json:"text"`
}

type span struct {
	Start  int `json:"start"`
	Length int `json:"length"`
}

type diagnostic struct {
	Code     string `json:"code"`
	Category string `json:"category"`
	Message  string `json:"message"`
	File     string `json:"file,omitempty"`
	Span     *span  `json:"span,omitempty"`
	Phase    string `json:"phase,omitempty"`
}

type artifact struct {
	Path    string `json:"path"`
	Content []byte `json:"content"`
}

type result struct {
	Diagnostics []diagnostic `json:"diagnostics"`
	Artifacts   []artifact   `json:"artifacts"`
	EmitSkipped bool         `json:"emitSkipped"`
}

type wireError struct {
	Code    string `json:"code"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
}

type envelope struct {
	APIVersion       int        `json:"apiVersion"`
	CompilerRevision string     `json:"compilerRevision"`
	Result           result     `json:"result"`
	Error            *wireError `json:"error,omitempty"`
}

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) == 2 && os.Args[1] == "--revision" {
		fmt.Println(compilerRevision)
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) == 2 && os.Args[1] == "--build-identity" {
		if err := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(struct {
			Revision    string `json:"revision"`
			PatchSeries string `json:"patchSeries"`
		}{Revision: compilerRevision, PatchSeries: compilerPatchSeries}); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		return
	}
	apiVersion, err := strconv.Atoi(bridgeAPIVersion)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "invalid embedded bridge API version")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	response := envelope{APIVersion: apiVersion, CompilerRevision: compilerRevision}
	decoder := json.NewDecoder(os.Stdin)
	decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
	var input request
	if err := decoder.Decode(&input); err != nil {
		response.Result.EmitSkipped = true
		response.Error = &wireError{Code: "SMITHERS_GO_PROTOCOL", Message: err.Error()}
	} else {
		var extra any
		if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
			response.Result.EmitSkipped = true
			response.Error = &wireError{Code: "SMITHERS_GO_PROTOCOL", Message: "expected one JSON request value"}
		} else {
			compiled, err := compile(context.Background(), input)
			response.Result = compiled
			if err != nil {
				response.Error = &wireError{Code: "SMITHERS_GO_COMPILE", Message: err.Error()}
			}
		}
	}
	if response.Result.Diagnostics == nil {
		response.Result.Diagnostics = []diagnostic{}
	}
	if response.Result.Artifacts == nil {
		response.Result.Artifacts = []artifact{}
	}
	if err := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout).Encode(response); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

type identityProject struct{}

func (identityProject) Refresh() error                                 { return nil }
func (identityProject) Identities() ([]string, error)                  { return []string{"smithers-poc@1"}, nil }
func (identityProject) Identity(*contentmapper.Mapper) (string, error) { return "smithers-poc@1", nil }
func (identityProject) WatchedFiles() ([]string, error)                { return nil, nil }
func (identityProject) Diagnostics() []contentmapper.OptionDiagnostic  { return nil }
func (identityProject) Close() error                                   { return nil }
func (identityProject) Transform(_ *contentmapper.Mapper, request contentmapper.Request) (contentmapper.Result, error) {
	segments := []spanmap.Segment(nil)
	if request.Content != "" {
		segments = []spanmap.Segment{{
			VirtualStart:  0,
			VirtualEnd:    core.TextPos(len(request.Content)),
			OriginalStart: 0,
			OriginalEnd:   core.TextPos(len(request.Content)),
			Kind:          spanmap.KindVerbatim,
			Features:      spanmap.FeatureAll,
		}}
	}
	return contentmapper.Result{
		Text:             request.Content,
		VirtualExtension: ".ts",
		Mappings:         spanmap.New(segments),
	}, nil
}

// mappingPoint is one decoded segment of an authored→lowered source map: a
// lowered (generated side) position and its optional authored origin. Columns
// are UTF-16 code units.
type mappingPoint struct {
	generatedCharacter int
	hasSource          bool
	sourceLine         int
	sourceCharacter    int
}

// smithersInput is one authored `.sm` compiler input together with its lowered
// TypeScript. In identity mode the lowered text is the authored text and the
// points describe a line-for-line identity mapping.
type smithersInput struct {
	logicalPath   string // request path, e.g. "dir/x.sm"
	authoredName  string // virtual authored name, e.g. "/src/dir/x.sm"
	loweredName   string // virtual lowered name, e.g. "/src/dir/x.sm.ts"
	authoredText  string
	loweredText   string
	authoredLines *lineIndex
	loweredLines  *lineIndex
	points        [][]mappingPoint // per lowered line, sorted by generatedCharacter
}

// project is the validated in-memory compilation unit shared by all modes.
type project struct {
	external          bool
	internal          bool
	smithersByLogical map[string]*smithersInput
	smithersByLowered map[string]*smithersInput
	assetByLogical    map[string]string // logical asset path → immutable source bytes
	assetByVirtual    map[string]string // virtual asset name → immutable source bytes
	assetModules      map[string]*compiledAssetModule
	tsTexts           map[string]string // virtual name → text for plain TypeScript inputs
	logicalByVirtual  map[string]string
	checkedFiles      map[string]string // authored names, identity checked program
	checkedRoots      []string
	emitFiles         map[string]string // lowered names, emit/external program
	emitRoots         []string
	renames           map[string]string // emitted "/out/..." path → final "/out/..." path
}

func compile(ctx context.Context, input request) (result, error) {
	if !bundled.Embedded {
		return result{EmitSkipped: true}, fmt.Errorf("the pinned compiler was built without embedded TypeScript libraries")
	}
	// The configuration gate runs before anything is built. A project whose
	// `tsconfig.json` violates §Mandatory or §Forbidden is not a project this
	// compiler can answer about, and answering anyway would be the fail-open
	// the specification's "MUST be rejected rather than ignored" forbids.
	if configDiagnostics := validateSmithersConfigFile(input.ConfigFile); len(configDiagnostics) > 0 {
		return result{EmitSkipped: true, Diagnostics: configDiagnostics}, nil
	}
	options, optionDiagnostics, err := compilerOptions(input.Options)
	if err != nil {
		return result{EmitSkipped: true}, err
	}
	if len(optionDiagnostics) > 0 {
		return result{EmitSkipped: true, Diagnostics: optionDiagnostics}, nil
	}
	project, err := buildProject(input)
	if err != nil {
		return result{EmitSkipped: true}, err
	}
	var compiled result
	if project.internal {
		compiled, err = compileInternal(ctx, options, project)
	} else if project.external {
		compiled, err = compileExternal(ctx, options, project)
	} else {
		compiled, err = compileIdentity(ctx, options, project)
	}
	// Every position inside the Go compiler and bridge is a byte offset. The
	// public compiler protocol, TypeScript APIs, editors, and LSP all use
	// absolute UTF-16 code-unit offsets. Convert exactly once, after every
	// parser/checker/lowering diagnostic has joined the result; converting in
	// individual producers would leave future diagnostic paths vulnerable to
	// the same global byte drift.
	project.convertDiagnosticSpansToUTF16(&compiled)
	// Migration step 5's second artifact, appended only when the request asked
	// for it and only when this compile emitted at all — a refused project must
	// keep emitting nothing, which several tests assert as `len(Artifacts) == 0`.
	if requestedEffectManifest && !compiled.EmitSkipped && len(durableManifestArtifacts) > 0 {
		compiled.Artifacts = append(compiled.Artifacts, durableManifestArtifacts...)
	}
	return compiled, err
}

func buildProject(input request) (*project, error) {
	external := false
	internal := false
	switch input.Lowering {
	case "":
		return nil, errors.New("lowering mode is required")
	case "identity":
	case "external":
		external = true
	case "internal":
		internal = true
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported lowering mode %q", input.Lowering)
	}

	built := &project{
		external:          external,
		internal:          internal,
		smithersByLogical: make(map[string]*smithersInput),
		smithersByLowered: make(map[string]*smithersInput),
		assetByLogical:    make(map[string]string),
		assetByVirtual:    make(map[string]string),
		assetModules:      make(map[string]*compiledAssetModule),
		tsTexts:           make(map[string]string),
		logicalByVirtual:  make(map[string]string),
		checkedFiles:      make(map[string]string),
		emitFiles:         make(map[string]string),
		renames:           make(map[string]string),
	}
	claim := func(virtualName string, logicalPath string) error {
		if _, exists := built.logicalByVirtual[virtualName]; exists {
			return fmt.Errorf("duplicate compiler input %q", logicalPath)
		}
		built.logicalByVirtual[virtualName] = logicalPath
		return nil
	}
	if internal {
		// The compiler-owned prelude is a real project input: it declares the
		// runtime representation of Result and publishes the Result type name
		// globally, so authored `.sm` files import nothing.
		if err := claim(preludeVirtualName, preludeLogicalPath); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		built.tsTexts[preludeVirtualName] = preludeText
		built.checkedFiles[preludeVirtualName] = preludeText
		built.emitFiles[preludeVirtualName] = preludeText
		built.checkedRoots = append(built.checkedRoots, preludeVirtualName)
		built.emitRoots = append(built.emitRoots, preludeVirtualName)

		// The comptime intrinsic lives in its own compiler-owned virtual
		// module rather than in the prelude. Every other compiler-owned
		// specifier is aliased to the prelude, so a shared file would make
		// `import { comptime } from "smithers:flows"` resolve to the real
		// intrinsic symbol. It is a declaration file, so it contributes
		// checker identity and no emitted artifact.
		if err := claim(comptimeVirtualName, comptimeLogicalPath); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		built.tsTexts[comptimeVirtualName] = comptimeDeclarationText
		built.checkedFiles[comptimeVirtualName] = comptimeDeclarationText
		built.emitFiles[comptimeVirtualName] = comptimeDeclarationText
		built.checkedRoots = append(built.checkedRoots, comptimeVirtualName)

		// Checker-only host declarations prevent an absent ambient @types/node
		// package from preempting Smithers's own host-module diagnostics. The
		// declarations remain foreign to the row analysis by design.
		if err := claim(hostModulesVirtualName, hostModulesLogicalPath); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		built.tsTexts[hostModulesVirtualName] = hostModulesDeclarationText
		built.checkedFiles[hostModulesVirtualName] = hostModulesDeclarationText
		built.emitFiles[hostModulesVirtualName] = hostModulesDeclarationText
		built.checkedRoots = append(built.checkedRoots, hostModulesVirtualName)
		built.emitRoots = append(built.emitRoots, hostModulesVirtualName)

		// Durable Flow declarations and runtime-safe Action bases have their
		// own module identity. The AST lowering rewrites imports to this emitted
		// virtual file after replacing durable(...) with a static Plan.
		if err := claim(durableVirtualName, durableLogicalPath); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		built.tsTexts[durableVirtualName] = durablePreludeText
		built.checkedFiles[durableVirtualName] = durablePreludeText
		built.emitFiles[durableVirtualName] = durablePreludeText
		built.checkedRoots = append(built.checkedRoots, durableVirtualName)
		built.emitRoots = append(built.emitRoots, durableVirtualName)
	}
	rootInputs := make(map[string]bool, len(input.RootNames))
	for _, rootName := range input.RootNames {
		rootInputs[rootName] = true
	}
	for _, file := range input.Files {
		authoredName, err := virtualFileName(file.Path)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if internal && (authoredName == preludeVirtualName || authoredName == comptimeVirtualName ||
			authoredName == hostModulesVirtualName ||
			authoredName == durableVirtualName) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("compiler input %q collides with the compiler-owned prelude", file.Path)
		}
		isSmithers := strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(file.Path), ".sm")
		// Protocol-v3 already publishes an explicit asset kind. Older harnesses
		// had to carry staged non-code files as "typescript" because this switch
		// did not accept that kind. Preserve measurement compatibility for those
		// requests only when the file is a non-root, non-code input; a real
		// TypeScript compilation root never changes meaning because of its
		// extension.
		isAsset := file.Kind == "asset" ||
			(file.Kind == "typescript" && !rootInputs[file.Path] && isPotentialAssetFilePath(file.Path))
		switch file.Kind {
		case "smithers":
			if !isSmithers {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("file %q has kind %q but not a .sm extension", file.Path, file.Kind)
			}
		case "typescript":
			if isSmithers {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("file %q has a .sm extension but kind %q", file.Path, file.Kind)
			}
		case "asset":
			if isSmithers {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("file %q has asset kind but a .sm extension", file.Path)
			}
		default:
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported file kind %q for %q", file.Kind, file.Path)
		}
		if isAsset {
			if file.Lowered != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("asset %q must not carry lowered content", file.Path)
			}
			if err := claim(authoredName, file.Path); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			built.assetByLogical[file.Path] = file.Text
			built.assetByVirtual[authoredName] = file.Text
			continue
		}
		if !isSmithers {
			if file.Lowered != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("file %q is not a .sm file and must not carry lowered content", file.Path)
			}
			if err := claim(authoredName, file.Path); err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			built.tsTexts[authoredName] = file.Text
			built.checkedFiles[authoredName] = file.Text
			built.emitFiles[authoredName] = file.Text
			continue
		}

		smithers := &smithersInput{
			logicalPath:   file.Path,
			authoredName:  authoredName,
			loweredName:   authoredName + ".ts",
			authoredText:  file.Text,
			authoredLines: newLineIndex(file.Text),
		}
		if external {
			if file.Lowered == nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("external lowering requires lowered content for .sm file %q", file.Path)
			}
			if file.Lowered.Text == "" {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("lowered text for %q is empty", file.Path)
			}
			smithers.loweredText = file.Lowered.Text
			smithers.loweredLines = newLineIndex(smithers.loweredText)
			if err := decodeSuppliedMap(smithers, file.Lowered.SourceMap); err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("lowered source map for %q: %w", file.Path, err)
			}
		} else {
			if file.Lowered != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("file %q carries lowered content but the request does not use \"external\" lowering", file.Path)
			}
			smithers.loweredText = file.Text
			smithers.loweredLines = smithers.authoredLines
			smithers.points = identityPoints(smithers.authoredLines)
		}
		if err := claim(authoredName, file.Path); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if err := claim(smithers.loweredName, file.Path); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		built.smithersByLogical[file.Path] = smithers
		built.smithersByLowered[smithers.loweredName] = smithers
		built.checkedFiles[authoredName] = file.Text
		built.emitFiles[smithers.loweredName] = smithers.loweredText

		trimmed := file.Path[:len(file.Path)-len(".sm")]
		built.renames["/out/"+trimmed+".sm.js"] = "/out/" + trimmed + ".js"
		built.renames["/out/"+trimmed+".sm.js.map"] = "/out/" + trimmed + ".js.map"
		built.renames["/out/"+trimmed+".sm.d.ts"] = "/out/" + trimmed + ".d.sm.ts"
		built.renames["/out/"+trimmed+".sm.d.ts.map"] = "/out/" + trimmed + ".d.sm.ts.map"
	}

	for _, rootName := range input.RootNames {
		authoredName, err := virtualFileName(rootName)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		logical, exists := built.logicalByVirtual[authoredName]
		if !exists || logical != rootName {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("root %q is absent from files", rootName)
		}
		if _, asset := built.assetByLogical[rootName]; asset {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("asset %q cannot be a compilation root", rootName)
		}
		built.checkedRoots = append(built.checkedRoots, authoredName)
		if smithers, ok := built.smithersByLogical[rootName]; ok {
			built.emitRoots = append(built.emitRoots, smithers.loweredName)
		} else {
			built.emitRoots = append(built.emitRoots, authoredName)
		}
	}
	return built, nil
}

func identityPoints(lines *lineIndex) [][]mappingPoint {
	points := make([][]mappingPoint, lines.lineCount())
	for line := range points {
		points[line] = []mappingPoint{{generatedCharacter: 0, hasSource: true, sourceLine: line, sourceCharacter: 0}}
	}
	return points
}

// suppliedSourceMap is the exact accepted field set for an authored→lowered
// version-3 source map. Unknown fields are rejected.
type suppliedSourceMap struct {
	Version        int       `json:"version"`
	File           string    `json:"file"`
	SourceRoot     string    `json:"sourceRoot"`
	Sources        []string  `json:"sources"`
	SourcesContent []*string `json:"sourcesContent"`
	Names          []string  `json:"names"`
	Mappings       *string   `json:"mappings"`
}

// decodeSuppliedMap validates an externally supplied authored→lowered source
// map against the authored and lowered texts and stores its mapping points.
func decodeSuppliedMap(smithers *smithersInput, mapText string) error {
	decoder := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(mapText))
	decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
	var parsed suppliedSourceMap
	if err := decoder.Decode(&parsed); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("parse: %w", err)
	}
	var extra any
	if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		return errors.New("parse: expected one JSON value")
	}
	if parsed.Version != 3 {
		return fmt.Errorf("version must be 3, got %d", parsed.Version)
	}
	if parsed.SourceRoot != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("sourceRoot must be empty, got %q", parsed.SourceRoot)
	}
	if len(parsed.Sources) != 1 {
		return fmt.Errorf("sources must name exactly the authored file, got %d entries", len(parsed.Sources))
	}
	if cleaned := path.Clean(parsed.Sources[0]); cleaned != path.Clean(smithers.logicalPath) {
		return fmt.Errorf("sources must name the authored file %q, got %q", smithers.logicalPath, parsed.Sources[0])
	}
	if parsed.SourcesContent != nil {
		if len(parsed.SourcesContent) != 1 || parsed.SourcesContent[0] == nil {
			return errors.New("sourcesContent must be exactly the authored text")
		}
		if *parsed.SourcesContent[0] != smithers.authoredText {
			return errors.New("sourcesContent does not match the supplied authored text")
		}
	}
	if parsed.Mappings == nil {
		return errors.New("mappings is required")
	}

	points := make([][]mappingPoint, smithers.loweredLines.lineCount())
	mappings := sourcemap.DecodeMappings(*parsed.Mappings)
	for mapping := range mappings.Values() {
		if mapping.GeneratedLine >= smithers.loweredLines.lineCount() {
			return fmt.Errorf("mapping targets lowered line %d beyond the lowered text", mapping.GeneratedLine)
		}
		if int(mapping.GeneratedCharacter) > smithers.loweredLines.utf16Length(mapping.GeneratedLine) {
			return fmt.Errorf("mapping targets lowered column %d beyond lowered line %d", mapping.GeneratedCharacter, mapping.GeneratedLine)
		}
		point := mappingPoint{generatedCharacter: int(mapping.GeneratedCharacter)}
		if mapping.IsSourceMapping() {
			if mapping.SourceIndex != 0 {
				return fmt.Errorf("mapping source index %d does not name the authored file", mapping.SourceIndex)
			}
			if mapping.SourceLine >= smithers.authoredLines.lineCount() {
				return fmt.Errorf("mapping targets authored line %d beyond the authored text", mapping.SourceLine)
			}
			if int(mapping.SourceCharacter) > smithers.authoredLines.utf16Length(mapping.SourceLine) {
				return fmt.Errorf("mapping targets authored column %d beyond authored line %d", mapping.SourceCharacter, mapping.SourceLine)
			}
			point.hasSource = true
			point.sourceLine = mapping.SourceLine
			point.sourceCharacter = int(mapping.SourceCharacter)
		} else if mapping.SourceIndex != sourcemap.MissingSource {
			return errors.New("mapping has a partial source position")
		}
		if mapping.NameIndex != sourcemap.MissingName && (mapping.NameIndex < 0 || int(mapping.NameIndex) >= len(parsed.Names)) {
			return fmt.Errorf("mapping name index %d is out of range", mapping.NameIndex)
		}
		points[mapping.GeneratedLine] = append(points[mapping.GeneratedLine], point)
	}
	if err := mappings.Error(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("mappings: %w", err)
	}
	for _, row := range points {
		sort.SliceStable(row, func(i, j int) bool { return row[i].generatedCharacter < row[j].generatedCharacter })
	}
	smithers.points = points
	return nil
}

// mapLoweredPosition maps a lowered (line, UTF-16 column) position to its
// authored counterpart: the greatest mapping on the same lowered line at or
// before the column, with the authored column advancing one-for-one within the
// mapping's run, clamped to the authored line end. Positions on lines without
// mappings, before the first mapping of their line, or inside a mapping that
// has no source are unmapped.
func mapLoweredPosition(smithers *smithersInput, line int, column int) (int, int, bool) {
	if line < 0 || line >= len(smithers.points) {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	row := smithers.points[line]
	index := sort.Search(len(row), func(i int) bool { return row[i].generatedCharacter > column }) - 1
	if index < 0 {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	point := row[index]
	if !point.hasSource {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	authoredColumn := point.sourceCharacter + (column - point.generatedCharacter)
	if limit := smithers.authoredLines.utf16Length(point.sourceLine); authoredColumn > limit {
		authoredColumn = limit
	}
	return point.sourceLine, authoredColumn, true
}

// mapLoweredSpan converts a lowered byte-offset span into an authored span.
// An unmapped start yields no span; an unmapped end keeps the lowered length,
// clamped to the authored text.
func (smithers *smithersInput) mapLoweredSpan(start int, length int) *span {
	startLine, startColumn := smithers.loweredLines.position(start)
	authoredLine, authoredColumn, ok := mapLoweredPosition(smithers, startLine, startColumn)
	if !ok {
		return nil
	}
	authoredStart := smithers.authoredLines.byteOffset(authoredLine, authoredColumn)
	endLine, endColumn := smithers.loweredLines.position(start + length)
	if mappedEndLine, mappedEndColumn, endOK := mapLoweredPosition(smithers, endLine, endColumn); endOK {
		if authoredEnd := smithers.authoredLines.byteOffset(mappedEndLine, mappedEndColumn); authoredEnd >= authoredStart {
			return &span{Start: authoredStart, Length: authoredEnd - authoredStart}
		}
	}
	if authoredStart+length > len(smithers.authoredText) {
		length = len(smithers.authoredText) - authoredStart
	}
	return &span{Start: authoredStart, Length: length}
}

func (p *project) convertDiagnostic(item *ast.Diagnostic, phase string) diagnostic {
	source := item.Source()
	if source == "" {
		source = "TS"
	}
	converted := diagnostic{
		Code:     source + strconv.FormatInt(int64(item.Code()), 10),
		Category: categoryName(item.Category()),
		Message:  item.Localize(locale.Default),
		Phase:    phase,
	}
	file := item.File()
	if file == nil {
		return converted
	}
	fileName := file.OriginalFileName()
	if smithers, ok := p.smithersByLowered[fileName]; ok {
		converted.File = smithers.logicalPath
		if item.Pos() >= 0 {
			converted.Span = smithers.mapLoweredSpan(item.Pos(), item.Len())
		}
		return converted
	}
	if logical, ok := p.logicalByVirtual[fileName]; ok {
		converted.File = logical
	} else {
		converted.File = strings.TrimPrefix(fileName, "/src/")
	}
	if item.Pos() >= 0 {
		converted.Span = &span{Start: item.Pos(), Length: item.Len()}
	}
	return converted
}

// sourceLines returns the authored line index named by a wire diagnostic. A
// Smithers diagnostic always targets authored text, never the lowered copy. A
// plain TypeScript or compiler-owned file has one virtual source identity.
func (p *project) sourceLines(logicalPath string) *lineIndex {
	if smithers := p.smithersByLogical[logicalPath]; smithers != nil {
		return smithers.authoredLines
	}
	if text, ok := p.assetByLogical[logicalPath]; ok {
		return newLineIndex(text)
	}
	for virtualName, candidate := range p.logicalByVirtual {
		if candidate != logicalPath {
			continue
		}
		if text, ok := p.tsTexts[virtualName]; ok {
			return newLineIndex(text)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// convertDiagnosticSpansToUTF16 enforces the compiler API's Span contract at
// the wire boundary. All span producers use fork AST/scanner positions, which
// are UTF-8 byte offsets. Both start and length must be converted: an astral
// character occupies four UTF-8 bytes but two UTF-16 units, while a combining
// mark remains its own UTF-16 unit rather than being folded into its base.
func (p *project) convertDiagnosticSpansToUTF16(compiled *result) {
	for index := range compiled.Diagnostics {
		item := &compiled.Diagnostics[index]
		if item.Span == nil {
			continue
		}
		lines := p.sourceLines(item.File)
		if lines == nil {
			continue
		}
		startByte := item.Span.Start
		endByte := startByte + item.Span.Length
		startUTF16 := lines.utf16Offset(startByte)
		endUTF16 := lines.utf16Offset(endByte)
		if endUTF16 < startUTF16 {
			endUTF16 = startUTF16
		}
		item.Span.Start = startUTF16
		item.Span.Length = endUTF16 - startUTF16
	}
}

type diagnosticCollector struct {
	project   *project
	converted []diagnostic
	seen      map[string]struct{}
}

func newDiagnosticCollector(p *project) *diagnosticCollector {
	return &diagnosticCollector{project: p, converted: make([]diagnostic, 0), seen: make(map[string]struct{})}
}

func (c *diagnosticCollector) add(phase string, items []*ast.Diagnostic) {
	for _, item := range items {
		c.addConverted(c.project.convertDiagnostic(item, phase))
	}
}

func (c *diagnosticCollector) addConverted(item diagnostic) {
	key := item.Code + "\x00" + item.File + "\x00" + item.Message
	if item.Span != nil {
		key += "\x00" + strconv.Itoa(item.Span.Start) + "\x00" + strconv.Itoa(item.Span.Length)
	}
	if _, exists := c.seen[key]; exists {
		return
	}
	c.seen[key] = struct{}{}
	c.converted = append(c.converted, item)
}

func (c *diagnosticCollector) collectProgram(ctx context.Context, program *compiler.Program) {
	c.add("parse", program.GetConfigFileParsingDiagnostics())
	c.add("parse", program.GetSyntacticDiagnostics(ctx, nil))
	c.add("bind", program.GetBindDiagnostics(ctx, nil))
	c.add("check", program.GetProgramDiagnostics())
	c.add("check", program.GetGlobalDiagnostics(ctx))
	c.add("check", program.GetSemanticDiagnostics(ctx, nil))
}

// compileIdentity checks authored `.sm` files through the fork's identity
// content mapper, emits mapped declarations from that Program, and runs the
// shared runtime emit pipeline over the (identical) lowered texts.
// newCheckProgram builds the Program over the authored `.sm` inputs, mapped
// through the fork's content-mapper extension registration. Identity lowering
// checks and emits declarations from it; internal lowering uses it to parse,
// bind, and resolve the types the Go lowering pass depends on.
func newCheckProgram(options *core.CompilerOptions, project *project) *compiler.Program {
	fs := bundled.WrapFS(vfstest.FromMap(project.checkedFiles, true))
	mapper := &contentmapper.Mapper{
		Definition: contentmapper.Definition{Package: "smithers", Extensions: []string{".sm"}},
		Manifest:   contentmapper.Manifest{Name: "smithers-poc", Version: "1"},
	}
	config := &tsoptions.ParsedCommandLine{ParsedConfig: &tsoptions.ParsedOptions{
		FileNames:       project.checkedRoots,
		CompilerOptions: options,
		ContentMappers:  []*contentmapper.Mapper{mapper},
	}}
	return compiler.NewProgram(compiler.ProgramOptions{
		Config:         config,
		Host:           compiler.NewCompilerHost("/src", fs, bundled.LibPath(), nil, nil, identityProject{}),
		SingleThreaded: core.TSTrue,
	})
}

func compileIdentity(ctx context.Context, options *core.CompilerOptions, project *project) (result, error) {
	program := newCheckProgram(options, project)

	collector := newDiagnosticCollector(project)
	collector.collectProgram(ctx, program)

	// Upstream deliberately delegates runtime output for content-mapped files
	// to the mapper/build tool, so this Program only owns declaration emit; the
	// shared emit pipeline below owns runtime JavaScript for all inputs.
	artifacts := make([]artifact, 0)
	if options.Declaration.IsTrue() && !options.NoEmit.IsTrue() {
		mappedEmit := program.Emit(ctx, compiler.EmitOptions{
			EmitOnly: compiler.EmitOnlyDts,
			WriteFile: func(fileName string, text string, _ *compiler.WriteFileData) error {
				artifacts = append(artifacts, artifact{Path: fileName, Content: []byte(text)})
				return nil
			},
		})
		collector.add("emit", mappedEmit.Diagnostics)
	}

	emitSkipped := true
	runEmit := !options.NoEmit.IsTrue() && (!options.NoEmitOnError.IsTrue() || !hasError(collector.converted))
	if runEmit {
		runtimeOptions := options.Clone()
		// Mapped declarations are emitted by the checked Program above. This
		// pass owns runtime JavaScript and its source map only.
		runtimeOptions.Declaration = core.TSFalse
		runtimeOptions.DeclarationMap = core.TSFalse
		runtimeOptions.EmitDeclarationOnly = core.TSFalse
		runtimeOptions.NoEmitOnError = core.TSFalse
		runtimeArtifacts, runtimeSkipped, err := runEmitProgram(ctx, runtimeOptions, project, collector, "emit")
		if err != nil {
			return result{Diagnostics: collector.converted, Artifacts: finishArtifacts(artifacts), EmitSkipped: true}, err
		}
		artifacts = append(artifacts, runtimeArtifacts...)
		emitSkipped = runtimeSkipped
	}
	finished := finishArtifacts(artifacts)
	if err := checkArtifactCollisions(finished); err != nil {
		return result{Diagnostics: collector.converted, Artifacts: []artifact{}, EmitSkipped: true}, err
	}
	return result{Diagnostics: collector.converted, Artifacts: finished, EmitSkipped: emitSkipped}, nil
}

// compileExternal checks externally lowered TypeScript through one fork
// Program, maps its diagnostics back to the authored `.sm` positions, and
// emits declarations plus runtime JavaScript whose source maps are composed
// with the supplied authored maps.
func compileExternal(ctx context.Context, options *core.CompilerOptions, project *project) (result, error) {
	collector := newDiagnosticCollector(project)
	checkProgram := newEmitProgram(options, project)
	collector.collectProgram(ctx, checkProgram)

	emitSkipped := true
	artifacts := make([]artifact, 0)
	runEmit := !options.NoEmit.IsTrue() && (!options.NoEmitOnError.IsTrue() || !hasError(collector.converted))
	if runEmit {
		raw := make([]artifact, 0)
		emit := checkProgram.Emit(ctx, compiler.EmitOptions{WriteFile: func(fileName string, text string, _ *compiler.WriteFileData) error {
			raw = append(raw, artifact{Path: fileName, Content: []byte(text)})
			return nil
		}})
		collector.add("emit", emit.Diagnostics)
		finalized, err := finalizeEmittedArtifacts(raw, project)
		if err != nil {
			return result{Diagnostics: collector.converted, Artifacts: []artifact{}, EmitSkipped: true}, err
		}
		artifacts = finalized
		emitSkipped = emit.EmitSkipped
	}
	finished := finishArtifacts(artifacts)
	if err := checkArtifactCollisions(finished); err != nil {
		return result{Diagnostics: collector.converted, Artifacts: []artifact{}, EmitSkipped: true}, err
	}
	return result{Diagnostics: collector.converted, Artifacts: finished, EmitSkipped: emitSkipped}, nil
}

// emitCompilerOptions is the check options with the EMIT-SHAPING members of
// compatibility.mdx §Mandatory cleared.
//
// §Mandatory governs the legality of authored `.sm`. It does not govern the
// shape of this compiler's own output, and three of its six members are not
// type rules at all: `verbatimModuleSyntax` and `isolatedModules` decide import
// elision, and `useDefineForClassFields` decides class-field semantics. Forcing
// them onto the emit Program was measured breaking a language guarantee rather
// than enforcing one — `import { type T } from "./sneaky.ts"` stopped being
// erased, so the named module's initializer RAN and
// `fork_module_closure_test.go`'s trust oracle printed
// "[reached] sneaky.ts initializer RAN". Smithers owns that erasure: a
// type-only import MUST NOT load the module it names, which is the opposite of
// what verbatim preservation produces.
//
// The same Program also carries the imported `.ts` and `.cts` a project names,
// and §Configuration is explicit that "Imported `.ts` and `.tsx` keep their own
// configuration. The escape-hatch guarantee in this page protects those files,
// not `.sm`." A `.cts` module written with `export function` is legal CommonJS
// TypeScript; under `verbatimModuleSyntax` it is TS1287, which is this compiler
// charging a foreign file for a rule the specification exempts it from.
//
// The two TYPE-level members stay on: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and
// `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` change what type-checks, never what is emitted,
// which is why the reference can hold its emitted module set to them too.
func emitCompilerOptions(options *core.CompilerOptions) *core.CompilerOptions {
	emit := options.Clone()
	emit.VerbatimModuleSyntax = core.TSUnknown
	emit.IsolatedModules = core.TSUnknown
	emit.UseDefineForClassFields = core.TSUnknown
	return emit
}

func newEmitProgram(options *core.CompilerOptions, project *project) *compiler.Program {
	options = emitCompilerOptions(options)
	fs := bundled.WrapFS(vfstest.FromMap(project.emitFiles, true))
	return compiler.NewProgram(compiler.ProgramOptions{
		Config: &tsoptions.ParsedCommandLine{ParsedConfig: &tsoptions.ParsedOptions{
			FileNames:       project.emitRoots,
			CompilerOptions: options,
		}},
		Host:           compiler.NewCompilerHost("/src", fs, bundled.LibPath(), nil, nil, nil),
		SingleThreaded: core.TSTrue,
	})
}

// runEmitProgram runs a fresh Program over the lowered file set, collecting
// its diagnostics under the given phase, and finalizes the emitted artifacts.
func runEmitProgram(ctx context.Context, options *core.CompilerOptions, project *project, collector *diagnosticCollector, phase string) ([]artifact, bool, error) {
	program := newEmitProgram(options, project)
	collector.add(phase, program.GetSyntacticDiagnostics(ctx, nil))
	collector.add(phase, program.GetSemanticDiagnostics(ctx, nil))
	raw := make([]artifact, 0)
	emit := program.Emit(ctx, compiler.EmitOptions{WriteFile: func(fileName string, text string, _ *compiler.WriteFileData) error {
		raw = append(raw, artifact{Path: fileName, Content: []byte(text)})
		return nil
	}})
	collector.add(phase, emit.Diagnostics)
	finalized, err := finalizeEmittedArtifacts(raw, project)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, true, err
	}
	return finalized, emit.EmitSkipped, nil
}

// specifierEdit is one replacement of a `.sm` import specifier inside an
// emitted JavaScript file, in pre-edit coordinates.
type specifierEdit struct {
	byteStart   int
	byteEnd     int
	replacement string
	line        int
	utf16Start  int
	utf16OldEnd int
	utf16NewLen int
}

// finalizeEmittedArtifacts rewrites relative `.sm` import specifiers in
// emitted JavaScript to their emitted `.js` names, renames `.sm`-derived
// outputs to their final artifact names, and composes every emitted source map
// back to the authored `.sm` sources.
func finalizeEmittedArtifacts(raw []artifact, project *project) ([]artifact, error) {
	editsByCodePath := make(map[string][]specifierEdit)
	for index := range raw {
		item := &raw[index]
		if strings.HasSuffix(item.Path, ".js") {
			text := string(item.Content)
			edits, err := planSpecifierEdits(project, item.Path, text)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			if len(edits) != 0 {
				editsByCodePath[item.Path] = edits
				text = applySpecifierEdits(text, edits)
			}
			if finalPath, renamed := project.renames[item.Path]; renamed {
				text = rewriteSourceMapURL(text, path.Base(item.Path)+".map", path.Base(finalPath)+".map")
			}
			item.Content = []byte(text)
			continue
		}
		if strings.HasSuffix(item.Path, ".d.ts") {
			if finalPath, renamed := project.renames[item.Path]; renamed {
				text := rewriteSourceMapURL(string(item.Content), path.Base(item.Path)+".map", path.Base(finalPath)+".map")
				item.Content = []byte(text)
			}
		}
	}
	for index := range raw {
		item := &raw[index]
		if !strings.HasSuffix(item.Path, ".map") {
			continue
		}
		codePath := strings.TrimSuffix(item.Path, ".map")
		finalCodePath := codePath
		if renamed, ok := project.renames[codePath]; ok {
			finalCodePath = renamed
		}
		composed, err := composeEmittedMap(project, item.Path, string(item.Content), editsByCodePath[codePath], path.Base(finalCodePath))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("compose source map %q: %w", item.Path, err)
		}
		item.Content = []byte(composed)
	}
	finalized := make([]artifact, 0, len(raw))
	for _, item := range raw {
		finalPath := item.Path
		if renamed, ok := project.renames[item.Path]; ok {
			finalPath = renamed
		}
		finalized = append(finalized, artifact{Path: finalPath, Content: item.Content})
	}
	return finalized, nil
}

// planSpecifierEdits parses one emitted JavaScript file with the fork parser
// and plans deterministic rewrites of relative import specifiers that end in
// `.sm` and name a project `.sm` input.
func planSpecifierEdits(project *project, artifactPath string, text string) ([]specifierEdit, error) {
	parsed := parser.ParseSourceFile(ast.SourceFileParseOptions{
		FileName: artifactPath,
		Path:     tspath.Path(artifactPath),
	}, text, core.ScriptKindJS)
	lines := newLineIndex(text)
	edits := make([]specifierEdit, 0)
	for _, literal := range parsed.Imports() {
		specifier := literal.Text()
		if !strings.HasPrefix(specifier, "./") && !strings.HasPrefix(specifier, "../") {
			continue
		}
		if !strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(specifier), ".sm") {
			continue
		}
		resolved := path.Clean(path.Join(path.Dir(artifactPath), specifier))
		logical := strings.TrimPrefix(resolved, "/out/")
		if _, known := project.smithersByLogical[logical]; !known {
			continue
		}
		start := scanner.SkipTrivia(text, literal.Pos())
		end := literal.End()
		if start < 0 || end > len(text) || end-start < 2 {
			continue
		}
		quoted := text[start:end]
		quote := quoted[0]
		if (quote != '"' && quote != '\'' && quote != '`') || quoted[len(quoted)-1] != quote {
			continue
		}
		if quoted[1:len(quoted)-1] != specifier {
			// The printed literal uses escapes; leave it untouched rather than
			// guess at its raw form.
			continue
		}
		replacement := string(quote) + specifier[:len(specifier)-len(".sm")] + ".js" + string(quote)
		startLine, startColumn := lines.position(start)
		endLine, endColumn := lines.position(end)
		if startLine != endLine {
			continue
		}
		edits = append(edits, specifierEdit{
			byteStart:   start,
			byteEnd:     end,
			replacement: replacement,
			line:        startLine,
			utf16Start:  startColumn,
			utf16OldEnd: endColumn,
			utf16NewLen: utf16Extent(replacement),
		})
	}
	sort.Slice(edits, func(i, j int) bool { return edits[i].byteStart < edits[j].byteStart })
	// SourceFile.Imports() can name one specifier more than once. The fork's
	// ForEachDynamicImportOrRequireCall finds candidate dynamic imports by
	// scanning the RAW TEXT for the substring "import"/"require" and resolving
	// the node at each hit, so every occurrence of those letters INSIDE a
	// dynamic import's own specifier resolves back to the same call and appends
	// the same literal again. A module whose file name merely contains the
	// letters "import" therefore produced two identical edits, and
	// applySpecifierEdits — which walks the sorted edits with one rising cursor
	// — panicked with `slice bounds out of range` and took the whole compile
	// down. Overlapping specifier spans are impossible in a well-formed plan, so
	// keeping the first of each overlapping run is both the crash fix and the
	// correct rewrite.
	deduplicated := edits[:0]
	previousEnd := -1
	for _, edit := range edits {
		if edit.byteStart < previousEnd {
			continue
		}
		deduplicated = append(deduplicated, edit)
		previousEnd = edit.byteEnd
	}
	return deduplicated, nil
}

func applySpecifierEdits(text string, edits []specifierEdit) string {
	var builder strings.Builder
	previous := 0
	for _, edit := range edits {
		builder.WriteString(text[previous:edit.byteStart])
		builder.WriteString(edit.replacement)
		previous = edit.byteEnd
	}
	builder.WriteString(text[previous:])
	return builder.String()
}

func rewriteSourceMapURL(text string, oldName string, newName string) string {
	return strings.ReplaceAll(text, "//# sourceMappingURL="+oldName, "//# sourceMappingURL="+newName)
}

// emittedSourceMap is the exact field set the pinned fork emits for a
// version-3 source map.
type emittedSourceMap struct {
	Version        int       `json:"version"`
	File           string    `json:"file"`
	SourceRoot     string    `json:"sourceRoot"`
	Sources        []string  `json:"sources"`
	Names          []string  `json:"names"`
	Mappings       string    `json:"mappings"`
	SourcesContent []*string `json:"sourcesContent"`
}

// composeEmittedMap composes a fork-emitted source map (generated artifact →
// lowered virtual file) with each `.sm` file's authored→lowered map so the
// final map's sources are the authored `.sm` files. Generated positions are
// first shifted across the specifier edits applied to the emitted text.
// Emitted positions whose lowered position is unmapped in the supplied map
// stay unmapped. Name entries are deliberately dropped: the authored names are
// not known to the bridge.
func composeEmittedMap(project *project, mapPath string, mapText string, edits []specifierEdit, finalFileBase string) (string, error) {
	decoder := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(mapText))
	decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
	var emitted emittedSourceMap
	if err := decoder.Decode(&emitted); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if emitted.Version != 3 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("emitted source map version %d is not 3", emitted.Version)
	}
	mapDirectory := path.Dir(mapPath)
	generator := sourcemap.NewGenerator(finalFileBase, "", mapDirectory, tspath.ComparePathsOptions{UseCaseSensitiveFileNames: true})
	includeContent := len(emitted.SourcesContent) != 0

	type sourceTarget struct {
		smithers *smithersInput
		index    sourcemap.SourceIndex
	}
	targets := make([]sourceTarget, len(emitted.Sources))
	for index, source := range emitted.Sources {
		resolved := path.Clean(path.Join(mapDirectory, source))
		if smithers, ok := project.smithersByLowered[resolved]; ok {
			generatorIndex := generator.AddSource(smithers.authoredName)
			if includeContent {
				if err := generator.SetSourceContent(generatorIndex, smithers.authoredText); err != nil {
					return "", err
				}
			}
			targets[index] = sourceTarget{smithers: smithers, index: generatorIndex}
			continue
		}
		generatorIndex := generator.AddSource(resolved)
		if includeContent {
			content := ""
			if text, ok := project.tsTexts[resolved]; ok {
				content = text
			} else if index < len(emitted.SourcesContent) && emitted.SourcesContent[index] != nil {
				content = *emitted.SourcesContent[index]
			}
			if err := generator.SetSourceContent(generatorIndex, content); err != nil {
				return "", err
			}
		}
		targets[index] = sourceTarget{index: generatorIndex}
	}

	editsByLine := make(map[int][]specifierEdit)
	for _, edit := range edits {
		editsByLine[edit.line] = append(editsByLine[edit.line], edit)
	}
	mappings := sourcemap.DecodeMappings(emitted.Mappings)
	for mapping := range mappings.Values() {
		generatedColumn := adjustGeneratedColumn(int(mapping.GeneratedCharacter), editsByLine[mapping.GeneratedLine])
		if !mapping.IsSourceMapping() {
			if err := generator.AddGeneratedMapping(mapping.GeneratedLine, core.UTF16Offset(generatedColumn)); err != nil {
				return "", err
			}
			continue
		}
		if int(mapping.SourceIndex) >= len(targets) {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("emitted mapping source index %d is out of range", mapping.SourceIndex)
		}
		target := targets[mapping.SourceIndex]
		if target.smithers == nil {
			if err := generator.AddSourceMapping(mapping.GeneratedLine, core.UTF16Offset(generatedColumn), target.index, mapping.SourceLine, mapping.SourceCharacter); err != nil {
				return "", err
			}
			continue
		}
		authoredLine, authoredColumn, ok := mapLoweredPosition(target.smithers, mapping.SourceLine, int(mapping.SourceCharacter))
		if !ok {
			if err := generator.AddGeneratedMapping(mapping.GeneratedLine, core.UTF16Offset(generatedColumn)); err != nil {
				return "", err
			}
			continue
		}
		if err := generator.AddSourceMapping(mapping.GeneratedLine, core.UTF16Offset(generatedColumn), target.index, authoredLine, core.UTF16Offset(authoredColumn)); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}
	if err := mappings.Error(); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	composed, err := json.Marshal(generator.RawSourceMap())
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return string(composed), nil
}

// adjustGeneratedColumn shifts a pre-edit UTF-16 column across the specifier
// edits applied to its line. Columns inside a replaced span clamp to the
// replacement start.
func adjustGeneratedColumn(column int, edits []specifierEdit) int {
	adjusted := column
	for _, edit := range edits {
		if column >= edit.utf16OldEnd {
			adjusted += edit.utf16NewLen - (edit.utf16OldEnd - edit.utf16Start)
			continue
		}
		if column > edit.utf16Start {
			adjusted -= column - edit.utf16Start
		}
		break
	}
	return adjusted
}

// finishArtifacts trims the virtual output prefix and orders artifacts.
func finishArtifacts(artifacts []artifact) []artifact {
	finished := make([]artifact, 0, len(artifacts))
	for _, item := range artifacts {
		finished = append(finished, artifact{Path: emittedFileName(item.Path), Content: item.Content})
	}
	// Emitted artifact paths derive from authored module paths, and this is the
	// order the caller receives the artifacts in.
	sortUTF16By(finished, func(item artifact) string { return item.Path })
	return finished
}

func checkArtifactCollisions(artifacts []artifact) error {
	seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(artifacts))
	for _, item := range artifacts {
		if _, exists := seen[item.Path]; exists {
			return fmt.Errorf("emitted artifact path collision at %q", item.Path)
		}
		seen[item.Path] = struct{}{}
	}
	return nil
}

func hasError(items []diagnostic) bool {
	for _, item := range items {
		if item.Category == "error" {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// smithersMandatoryOptions mirrors MANDATORY_COMPILER_OPTIONS in
// poc/src/language/compiler-options.ts, which mirrors compatibility.mdx
// §Mandatory. compiler/forkbridge_options_test.go fails if the two drift.
var smithersMandatoryOptions = []string{
	"strict",
	"noUncheckedIndexedAccess",
	"exactOptionalPropertyTypes",
	"isolatedModules",
	"verbatimModuleSyntax",
	"useDefineForClassFields",
}

// smithersForbiddenOptions mirrors FORBIDDEN_COMPILER_OPTIONS in
// poc/src/language/compiler-options.ts, which mirrors compatibility.mdx
// §Forbidden.
var smithersForbiddenOptions = []string{
	"keyofStringsOnly",
	"suppressImplicitAnyIndexErrors",
	"suppressExcessPropertyErrors",
	"noStrictGenericChecks",
	"noImplicitUseStrict",
	"out",
	"charset",
	"importsNotUsedAsValues",
	"preserveValueImports",
	"experimentalDecorators",
	"emitDecoratorMetadata",
}

// smithersPermittedOptions mirrors PERMITTED_COMPILER_OPTIONS in
// poc/src/language/compiler-options.ts: compatibility.mdx §Emit-Scoped plus the
// project-layout and additional-soundness names a Smithers project MAY state. A
// project MAY tighten beyond §Mandatory; it MUST NOT loosen below it.
var smithersPermittedOptions = []string{
	"target",
	"lib",
	"module",
	"moduleResolution",
	"jsx",
	"downlevelIteration",
	"importHelpers",
	"esModuleInterop",
	"allowSyntheticDefaultImports",
	"rootDir",
	"outDir",
	"baseUrl",
	"paths",
	"types",
	"typeRoots",
	"declaration",
	"declarationMap",
	"declarationDir",
	"sourceMap",
	"inlineSources",
	"inlineSourceMap",
	"noEmit",
	"noEmitOnError",
	"emitDeclarationOnly",
	"removeComments",
	"newLine",
	"preserveConstEnums",
	"incremental",
	"composite",
	"tsBuildInfoFile",
	"skipLibCheck",
	"skipDefaultLibCheck",
	"allowJs",
	"checkJs",
	"resolveJsonModule",
	"allowImportingTsExtensions",
	"rewriteRelativeImportExtensions",
	"forceConsistentCasingInFileNames",
	"moduleDetection",
	"allowArbitraryExtensions",
	"customConditions",
	"noErrorTruncation",
	"pretty",
	"noImplicitOverride",
	"noImplicitReturns",
	"noFallthroughCasesInSwitch",
	"noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature",
	"noUnusedLocals",
	"noUnusedParameters",
	"allowUnreachableCode",
	"allowUnusedLabels",
	"strictNullChecks",
	"strictFunctionTypes",
	"strictBindCallApply",
	"strictPropertyInitialization",
	"strictBuiltinIteratorReturn",
	"noImplicitAny",
	"noImplicitThis",
	"alwaysStrict",
	"useUnknownInCatchVariables",
	"comptimeTarget",
	"smithersEffectManifest",
}

// isKnownSmithersOption reports whether a Smithers project may mention `name`
// in its `tsconfig.json` at all. An option nobody has classified is not
// silently honored — see rejectedOption's SMITHERS6003 arm.
func isKnownSmithersOption(name string) bool {
	for _, known := range smithersPermittedOptions {
		if known == name {
			return true
		}
	}
	for _, known := range smithersMandatoryOptions {
		if known == name {
			return true
		}
	}
	return isForbiddenOption(name)
}

func isForbiddenOption(name string) bool {
	for _, forbidden := range smithersForbiddenOptions {
		if forbidden == name {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// requiredOption is SMITHERS6001: a §Mandatory option was stated with a value
// other than `true`.
func requiredOption(name string) diagnostic {
	return diagnostic{
		Code:     "SMITHERS6001",
		Category: "error",
		Message:  fmt.Sprintf("a Smithers project MUST set '%s: true'", name),
	}
}

// rejectedOption is the coded form of the allowlist's default arm:
// SMITHERS6002 when the specification names the option as forbidden,
// SMITHERS6003 when nothing classifies it and the fail-closed reading of
// §Forbidden's "MUST be rejected rather than ignored" applies.
func rejectedOption(name string) diagnostic {
	if isForbiddenOption(name) {
		return diagnostic{
			Code:     "SMITHERS6002",
			Category: "error",
			Message: fmt.Sprintf(
				"'%s' is a forbidden compiler option in a Smithers project and MUST be removed rather than set to a value",
				name),
		}
	}
	return diagnostic{
		Code:     "SMITHERS6003",
		Category: "error",
		Message:  fmt.Sprintf("unsupported compiler option '%s' in a Smithers project", name),
	}
}

// validateSmithersConfigFile is the fork's half of the tsconfig gate, and the
// half that carries spans.
//
// It parses the configuration as JSON with the fork's own parser, so an
// offending option is reported at the position the author wrote it — which is
// what compatibility.mdx §Forbidden's "MUST be rejected rather than ignored"
// needs and what the previous `fmt.Errorf("unsupported compiler option %q")`
// could not give. The rule set is validateSmithersTsconfig's in
// poc/src/language/compiler-options.ts, case for case, because `.sm` legality
// may not depend on which backend compiled it.
//
// Offsets are converted to UTF-16 here rather than by
// convertDiagnosticSpansToUTF16. That converter maps spans through the PROJECT's
// files, and a `tsconfig.json` is not one of them — it is never staged, never
// lowered, and has no logical name. Converting locally is the only place the
// configuration's own text is in scope.
func validateSmithersConfigFile(config *configFile) []diagnostic {
	if config == nil {
		return nil
	}
	parsed := parser.ParseSourceFile(ast.SourceFileParseOptions{
		FileName: config.Path,
		Path:     tspath.Path(config.Path),
	}, config.Text, core.ScriptKindJSON)
	diagnostics := make([]diagnostic, 0)
	at := func(code string, message string, start int, length int) {
		utf16Start := len(utf16.Encode([]rune(config.Text[:start])))
		utf16Length := len(utf16.Encode([]rune(config.Text[start : start+length])))
		diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnostic{
			Code:     code,
			Category: "error",
			Message:  message,
			File:     config.Path,
			Span:     &span{Start: utf16Start, Length: utf16Length},
		})
	}
	nodeSpan := func(node *ast.Node) (int, int) {
		start := scanner.SkipTrivia(config.Text, node.Pos())
		return start, node.End() - start
	}

	var options *ast.Node
	if len(parsed.Statements.Nodes) > 0 {
		root := parsed.Statements.Nodes[0].Expression()
		if root != nil && ast.IsObjectLiteralExpression(root) {
			for _, property := range root.AsObjectLiteralExpression().Properties.Nodes {
				if !ast.IsPropertyAssignment(property) {
					continue
				}
				name := property.Name()
				if name == nil || !ast.IsStringLiteral(name) || name.Text() != "compilerOptions" {
					continue
				}
				if initializer := property.AsPropertyAssignment().Initializer; initializer != nil &&
					ast.IsObjectLiteralExpression(initializer) {
					options = initializer
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if options == nil {
		for _, name := range smithersMandatoryOptions {
			at("SMITHERS6001",
				fmt.Sprintf("a Smithers project MUST set '%s: true'; this tsconfig has no compilerOptions", name),
				0, max(1, len(config.Text)))
		}
		return diagnostics
	}

	stated := make(map[string]*ast.Node)
	for _, property := range options.AsObjectLiteralExpression().Properties.Nodes {
		if !ast.IsPropertyAssignment(property) {
			continue
		}
		name := property.Name()
		if name == nil || !ast.IsStringLiteral(name) {
			continue
		}
		stated[name.Text()] = property
		start, length := nodeSpan(name)
		if isForbiddenOption(name.Text()) {
			at("SMITHERS6002", rejectedOption(name.Text()).Message, start, length)
			continue
		}
		if !isKnownSmithersOption(name.Text()) {
			at("SMITHERS6003", rejectedOption(name.Text()).Message, start, length)
		}
	}

	objectStart, objectLength := nodeSpan(options)
	for _, name := range smithersMandatoryOptions {
		property, ok := stated[name]
		if !ok {
			at("SMITHERS6001", requiredOption(name).Message, objectStart, objectLength)
			continue
		}
		initializer := property.AsPropertyAssignment().Initializer
		if initializer == nil || initializer.Kind != ast.KindTrueKeyword {
			start, _ := nodeSpan(property.Name())
			end := property.End()
			at("SMITHERS6001", requiredOption(name).Message, start, end-start)
		}
	}
	return diagnostics
}

func compilerOptions(raw map[string]any) (*core.CompilerOptions, []diagnostic, error) {
	options := &core.CompilerOptions{
		Target:           core.ScriptTargetES2022,
		Module:           core.ModuleKindESNext,
		ModuleResolution: core.ModuleResolutionKindBundler,
		RootDir:          "/src",
		OutDir:           "/out",
		SkipLibCheck:     core.TSTrue,
		// compatibility.mdx §Mandatory, in full. `Strict` was the only member
		// of that table this bridge set, which made the fork and the reference
		// agree on `strict` and silently disagree on the other five. They are
		// defaults rather than caller options because §Configuration forbids
		// them to vary: "Soundness settings MUST therefore be mandatory and
		// MUST NOT vary by JavaScript host." The allowlist below still ACCEPTS
		// each name, so a caller may state the obligation explicitly, but the
		// value it may state is `true`.
		Strict:                     core.TSTrue,
		NoUncheckedIndexedAccess:   core.TSTrue,
		ExactOptionalPropertyTypes: core.TSTrue,
		IsolatedModules:            core.TSTrue,
		VerbatimModuleSyntax:       core.TSTrue,
		UseDefineForClassFields:    core.TSTrue,
		// Smithers requires a TypeScript module to be imported by its authored
		// `./x.ts` spelling — that spelling is what the module-initialization
		// trust check resolves — so this is a language default, not a caller
		// preference. Upstream pairs it with the extension rewrite below.
		AllowImportingTsExtensions: core.TSTrue,
		SourceMap:                  core.TSTrue,
		InlineSources:              core.TSTrue,
		NoEmitOnError:              core.TSTrue,
	}
	rejections := make([]diagnostic, 0)
	// Sorted so a request carrying several rejected options reports them in a
	// stable order; Go map iteration is randomized per run and a diagnostic
	// list that reordered between identical compiles would break every
	// expectation that names more than one.
	//
	// sortUTF16 rather than sort.Strings, and that is not a formality here. The
	// names in this map are CALLER-SUPPLIED — admitting an unclassified one is
	// the whole point of SMITHERS6003 — and this order is OBSERVED, as the order
	// of the diagnostics the caller receives. That is precisely the combination
	// `TestPinnedForkBridgeByteOrderSortsAreReviewed` exists to keep out of a
	// byte-order sort, so this site is not added to its census; it is moved off
	// the comparator the census guards.
	names := make([]string, 0, len(raw))
	for name := range raw {
		names = append(names, name)
	}
	sortUTF16(names)
	for _, name := range names {
		value := raw[name]
		switch name {
		case "sourceMap":
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			options.SourceMap = parsed
		case "inlineSources":
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			options.InlineSources = parsed
		case "declaration":
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			options.Declaration = parsed
		case "declarationMap":
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			options.DeclarationMap = parsed
		case "noEmitOnError":
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			options.NoEmitOnError = parsed
		case "noEmit":
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			options.NoEmit = parsed
		// compatibility.mdx §Mandatory. Each is ACCEPTED so a project may state
		// the obligation explicitly, and each is pinned to `true` so stating it
		// cannot weaken it: `strict: false` used to be honored here, which made
		// the one mandatory option this bridge did set caller-defeasible.
		case "strict", "noUncheckedIndexedAccess", "exactOptionalPropertyTypes",
			"isolatedModules", "verbatimModuleSyntax", "useDefineForClassFields":
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			if !parsed.IsTrue() {
				rejections = append(rejections, requiredOption(name))
			}
		case "allowImportingTsExtensions":
			// A `.sm` file that names a TypeScript module by its authored
			// `./x.ts` spelling is how module-initialization trust is checked;
			// without this the fork reports TS5097 for the very spelling the
			// language requires.
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			options.AllowImportingTsExtensions = parsed
		case "rewriteRelativeImportExtensions":
			parsed, err := tristate(value)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, err)
			}
			options.RewriteRelativeImportExtensions = parsed
		case "target":
			text, ok := value.(string)
			if !ok {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, fmt.Errorf("must be a string"))
			}
			switch strings.ToLower(text) {
			case "es2015":
				options.Target = core.ScriptTargetES2015
			case "es2020":
				options.Target = core.ScriptTargetES2020
			case "es2022":
				options.Target = core.ScriptTargetES2022
			case "esnext":
				options.Target = core.ScriptTargetESNext
			default:
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, fmt.Errorf("unsupported value %q", text))
			}
		case "comptimeTarget":
			// The typed target value `comptime.target` exposes. It is a
			// declared compiler input, not ambient process state, so a
			// target-selected branch stays hermetic and reproducible.
			text, ok := value.(string)
			if !ok || text == "" {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, fmt.Errorf("must be a non-empty string"))
			}
			requestedComptimeTarget = text
		case "smithersEffectManifest":
			// Migration step 5. Asks the durable lowering to publish each
			// Flow's Effect Manifest, and the Plan it was NOT derived from,
			// as two extra JSON artifacts so a cross-check can compare them.
			// Absent — every existing caller — nothing is derived and nothing
			// is emitted.
			parsed, ok := value.(bool)
			if !ok {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, fmt.Errorf("must be a boolean"))
			}
			requestedEffectManifest = parsed
		case "module":
			text, ok := value.(string)
			if !ok {
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, fmt.Errorf("must be a string"))
			}
			switch strings.ToLower(text) {
			case "esnext":
				options.Module = core.ModuleKindESNext
				options.ModuleResolution = core.ModuleResolutionKindBundler
			case "commonjs":
				options.Module = core.ModuleKindCommonJS
				options.ModuleResolution = core.ModuleResolutionKindNode10
			default:
				return nil, nil, optionError(name, fmt.Errorf("unsupported value %q", text))
			}
		default:
			// The arm that used to be `fmt.Errorf("unsupported compiler option
			// %q", name)` — a bare string travelling in the envelope's Error
			// field rather than in Result.Diagnostics, so it reached the CLI
			// with no code, no file and no span, and acquired only the generic
			// SMITHERS_GO_BACKEND at the outermost layer. The allowlist itself
			// is kept: it was already the only option chokepoint either backend
			// had. What is added is the classification the specification draws,
			// so a forbidden option is refused as forbidden rather than as
			// unknown.
			rejections = append(rejections, rejectedOption(name))
		}
	}
	if options.DeclarationMap.IsTrue() {
		options.Declaration = core.TSTrue
	}
	// Upstream accepts `allowImportingTsExtensions` only alongside one of
	// `noEmit`, `emitDeclarationOnly`, or `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`
	// (`internal/compiler/program.go:1270`). This mode emits runtime
	// JavaScript, so the authored `./x.ts` specifier has to become `./x.js` in
	// the output, which is exactly what the third option does.
	if options.AllowImportingTsExtensions.IsTrue() && !options.NoEmit.IsTrue() && !options.EmitDeclarationOnly.IsTrue() {
		options.RewriteRelativeImportExtensions = core.TSTrue
	}
	return options, rejections, nil
}

func tristate(value any) (core.Tristate, error) {
	parsed, ok := value.(bool)
	if !ok {
		return core.TSUnknown, fmt.Errorf("must be a boolean")
	}
	if parsed {
		return core.TSTrue, nil
	}
	return core.TSFalse, nil
}

func optionError(name string, err error) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("compiler option %q %w", name, err)
}

func virtualFileName(logical string) (string, error) {
	logical = strings.ReplaceAll(logical, "\\", "/")
	if strings.HasPrefix(logical, "/") || strings.Contains(logical, ":") {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("compiler input path %q must be relative", logical)
	}
	clean := path.Clean(logical)
	if clean == "." || clean == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(clean, "../") {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("compiler input path %q escapes the virtual project", logical)
	}
	return "/src/" + clean, nil
}

func emittedFileName(fileName string) string {
	fileName = strings.ReplaceAll(fileName, "\\", "/")
	return strings.TrimPrefix(fileName, "/out/")
}

func categoryName(category diagnostics.Category) string {
	switch category {
	case diagnostics.CategoryWarning:
		return "warning"
	case diagnostics.CategoryError:
		return "error"
	case diagnostics.CategorySuggestion:
		return "suggestion"
	case diagnostics.CategoryMessage:
		return "message"
	default:
		return "error"
	}
}

// lineIndex converts between byte offsets and (line, UTF-16 column) positions
// of one immutable text. Lines split on '\n'; a '\r' before it belongs to the
// preceding line's content.
type lineIndex struct {
	text   string
	starts []int
}

func newLineIndex(text string) *lineIndex {
	starts := []int{0}
	for offset := 0; offset < len(text); offset++ {
		if text[offset] == '\n' {
			starts = append(starts, offset+1)
		}
	}
	return &lineIndex{text: text, starts: starts}
}

func (index *lineIndex) lineCount() int { return len(index.starts) }

func (index *lineIndex) lineText(line int) string {
	if line < 0 || line >= len(index.starts) {
		return ""
	}
	start := index.starts[line]
	end := len(index.text)
	if line+1 < len(index.starts) {
		end = index.starts[line+1] - 1
	}
	return index.text[start:end]
}

func (index *lineIndex) utf16Length(line int) int {
	return utf16Extent(index.lineText(line))
}

func (index *lineIndex) position(byteOffset int) (line int, utf16Column int) {
	if byteOffset < 0 {
		byteOffset = 0
	}
	if byteOffset > len(index.text) {
		byteOffset = len(index.text)
	}
	low, high := 0, len(index.starts)-1
	for low < high {
		middle := (low + high + 1) / 2
		if index.starts[middle] <= byteOffset {
			low = middle
		} else {
			high = middle - 1
		}
	}
	return low, utf16Extent(index.text[index.starts[low]:byteOffset])
}

func (index *lineIndex) byteOffset(line int, utf16Column int) int {
	if line < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if line >= len(index.starts) {
		return len(index.text)
	}
	lineText := index.lineText(line)
	consumed := 0
	for byteAt, character := range lineText {
		if consumed >= utf16Column {
			return index.starts[line] + byteAt
		}
		consumed += utf16RuneLen(character)
	}
	return index.starts[line] + len(lineText)
}

// utf16Offset converts one absolute UTF-8 byte offset into the absolute
// UTF-16 code-unit offset required by the compiler transport. It deliberately
// counts code points rather than grapheme clusters: a combining sequence has
// one unit for the base and one for its combining mark, matching TypeScript.
func (index *lineIndex) utf16Offset(byteOffset int) int {
	if byteOffset < 0 {
		byteOffset = 0
	}
	if byteOffset > len(index.text) {
		byteOffset = len(index.text)
	}
	return utf16Extent(index.text[:byteOffset])
}

func utf16Extent(text string) int {
	length := 0
	for _, character := range text {
		length += utf16RuneLen(character)
	}
	return length
}

func utf16RuneLen(character rune) int {
	if character > 0xFFFF {
		return 2
	}
	return 1
}
